title: storage/archive: fix overlay whiteout ID mappings
body:
# storage: convert overlay whiteouts before mapping ownership

Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/issues/1170

## Problem

With native overlay storage and `--uidmap 0:1:65535 --gidmap 0:1:65535`, an
unsquashed Podman commit can succeed while omitting deletions. Removed files and
directories then reappear when the image is used, including after save/load into
an empty store.

Native overlay represents a deletion as a character device `0:0`. These markers
can be owned by IDs outside the container's mapping. `prepareAddFile` currently
maps ownership before converting the marker into a `.wh.*` archive entry. The
existing filename-based exemption therefore does not recognize the native
marker, and the archive walker logs the mapping error and skips it:

```text
Can't add file <upperdir>/whiteout-repro/remove-file to tar: host ID 0 cannot be mapped to a container ID; skipping
```

## Solution

Convert native whiteouts before deciding whether ordinary ownership mapping
applies. Set converted whiteout ownership to `0:0`, then apply any explicit
`ChownOpts` override.

An opaque directory hides its lower-layer contents using a separate synthetic
archive marker. Copy the directory's finalized IDs and names to that marker so
it retains the same ownership behavior after the reordered conversion.

## Changes

- `storage/pkg/archive/archive.go`: move whiteout conversion ahead of ID mapping
  and finalize synthetic opaque-marker ownership after mapping and overrides.
- `storage/pkg/archive/archive_linux.go`: normalize converted whiteout IDs to zero.
- `storage/pkg/archive/archive_linux_test.go`: cover root and nonzero whiteout
  owners, separately unmapped UID/GID, mapped IDs, explicit ownership overrides,
  normal file/directory ownership and opaque markers.

This addresses whiteout handling; the archive walker's broader log-and-continue
error policy is unchanged.

## Verification

Tested on Linux amd64, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-111-generic, native overlay/XFS,
with rootful Podman inside an outer user namespace and Go 1.26.4.

The patch applies unchanged to both the main commit above and `storage/v1.64.0`,
commit `3aa788d1726dc0455117a1cc6290fffa14104f35` ("Bump c/storage to v1.64.0").

### Archive tests

Identical regression tests were compiled against original and patched production
code on both storage refs. All seven whiteout cases fail before and pass after.
Normal file/directory, opaque-marker and invalid normal-entry ID controls pass.

The candidate main test binary was run as root with:

```sh
./whiteout-main-after.test -test.v -test.count=1 \
  -test.run 'TestOverlayTar(Whiteout|FileAndDirectory)IDMappings|TestPrepareAddFileUnmappedIDs'
./whiteout-main-after.test -test.v -test.count=1
go vet ./storage/pkg/archive
```

Equivalent before/after binaries were run for the pinned storage release.
`gofumpt v0.9.2` and `git diff --check` also passed.

Full patched archive-package results:

| Source | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 96 | 1 | 0 |
| storage/v1.64.0 | 94 | 1 | 0 |

The existing `TestTarWithBlockCharFifo` fails with `EPERM` when creating block
device `12:5` in the outer user namespace, on both original and patched code.
The new character-device `0:0` whiteout tests execute successfully. The complete
monorepo test/lint gate was not run; the full archive-package gate remains
non-green because of this test-host limitation.

### Podman commit/save/load

Podman 6.1.1, commit `8303f2e25b675ea7f82099d615c60969aec15870`
("Bump to v6.1.1"), was rebuilt with and without the patch using the same tags:

```sh
make bin/podman \
  BUILDTAGS='seccomp systemd exclude_graphdriver_btrfs containers_image_openpgp'
```

The candidate additionally used Go's compiler overlay for the two patched source
files, after checking their original versions matched Podman's vendored storage
source byte-for-byte.

Each case checks the committed image directly and after save/load into an empty
store:

| Case | Original | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Unmapped, unsquashed | Pass | Pass |
| Unmapped, squashed | Pass | Pass |
| Mapped, unsquashed | File, directory and nested-file deletions lost | Pass |
| Mapped, squashed | Pass | Pass |

Consumer filesystem checks improve from **42/48** to **48/48**. The mapped
unsquashed delta contains zero whiteouts before the fix and all three expected
whiteouts afterwards. Producer absence, additions, modifications and unchanged
contents were also checked.

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproducer: exits 1 before the patch and 0 afterwards</summary>

Run as root on a disposable Linux host with native overlay storage. The script
creates uniquely named containers/images and removes them on exit. The image
digest was tested through a registry mirror; the direct public registry endpoint
was not exercised in that environment.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [[ $(id -u) != 0 ]]; then
    printf 'Run on a disposable rootful Podman test host.\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi

podman="${PODMAN:-podman}"
image="${IMAGE:-docker.io/library/alpine@sha256:7c8cb692ae09657cbc4a3f3cbd0e8d5a2690ba38386aaaf252dbb060bf5eb2e6}"
token="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/whiteout-repro.XXXXXXXX")"
name="$(basename "$token" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr . -)"
base_container="$name-base"
changed_container="$name-changed"
base_image="localhost/$name:base"
changed_image="localhost/$name:changed"
cleanup() {
    "$podman" rm --force "$base_container" "$changed_container" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "$podman" rmi "$changed_image" "$base_image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    rmdir "$token"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

"$podman" version
"$podman" run --name "$base_container" --network none \
    --entrypoint /bin/sh "$image" -ec \
    'mkdir -p /whiteout-repro/remove-dir; printf old > /whiteout-repro/remove-file; printf old > /whiteout-repro/remove-dir/file'
"$podman" commit --format oci "$base_container" "$base_image"

"$podman" run --name "$changed_container" --network none \
    --uidmap 0:1:65535 --gidmap 0:1:65535 \
    --entrypoint /bin/sh "$base_image" -ec \
    'rm /whiteout-repro/remove-file; rm -r /whiteout-repro/remove-dir; test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-file; test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-dir'

"$podman" diff "$changed_container"
"$podman" commit --format oci --squash=false "$changed_container" "$changed_image"

"$podman" run --rm --network none \
    --uidmap 0:1:65535 --gidmap 0:1:65535 \
    --entrypoint /bin/sh "$changed_image" -ec \
    'test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-file; test ! -e /whiteout-repro/remove-dir; printf "Deletion markers preserved\n"'
```

</details>
